descriptor: Quarterly almanac of small rockets and the people behind them

voice.summary: Starling Almanac writes with the nerdy affection of a space-history society newsletter. Countdowns, mission names and tiny engineering anecdotes carry the story, with a wink at near-failures.
dos: Use mission names and dates as hooks
Tell the story of the engineers, not just the hardware
Keep a dry countdown rhythm: three, two, one
donts: Do not use space-race hype or 'to infinity' puns
Never sound like a launch-day press release

taglines: Every launch begins with a countdown
The missions that nearly did not fly
History from the launch pad up
boilerplate: Starling Almanac is a quarterly publication celebrating small rockets, patient engineers and the missions that nearly did not fly, from Lantern-1 to the Tern Relay.

microcopy.success: Liftoff. You are back at the top.

microcopy.empty: No missions in this issue yet.

logo.note: A rocket is the obvious and joyful symbol for an almanac of small launches and a footer that blasts off.
